newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador says to issue up to $250 mln in bonds.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador says to issue up to $250 mln in bonds.

text.p: Ecuador's government is going to issue up to $250 million of bonds in order to make a partial payment of debt owed to the Paris Club of creditor nations, a government official said Friday.

"Through a decree to be signed by the government today, we will issue up to $250 million in bonds that will be used to restructure domestic credit liabilities and to partially pay off debt with the Paris Club," an official at the Finance Ministry, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.
The official said interest on the bonds would be the prime rate plus one percentage point. The maturities would be between three and five years.
He did not say whether the Paris Club payments would be to pay off interest or principal.
The official said it was hoped some $120 million of the planned bonds would be placed in the local market Thursday.
The government of President Fabian Alarcon is currently negotiating with the Paris Club for a restructuring of the $1.2 billion of debt Ecuador has with the organization.
Recently Ecuador carried out a Brady debt buyback with the proceeds of its first ever Eurobond issue, of $500 million.
